detail.what_worked: Re-measuring against symbol names/quoted strings (per the task's line-number caveat) rather than trusting the baseline's counts let two genuine additional defects surface (temp-path collision, non-atomic python3 writes) that a pure confirmation pass would have missed.
detail.what_was_hard: Distinguishing 'script-level' writer counts (baseline's framing) from 'call-site-level' counts (what the implementer actually needs to enumerate) required reading full file bodies rather than grepping for the mv/tmp idiom alone, since two sites used python3 with no temp file at all and would not match a naive grep for the shared-path pattern.
detail.what_was_missed: Did not verify the extension-wide inline SKILL.md writers in the same depth as the core file_scope (correctly out of scope per file_scope, but flagged only at a survey level, not per-file).
detail.successes: Verified, with a concrete caller audit, that the task-lock.sh release ownership check is safe to add without breaking any of the 5 existing call sites -- this was a stated risk in the task description that research was able to resolve rather than leave open.
